question: Define emf and terminal potential difference of a cell. Obtain the relation $V=\varepsilon-Ir$ for a cell supplying current and calculate $V$ for $\varepsilon=2.0\,\text{V}$, $I=0.5\,\text{A}$ and $r=0.4\,\Omega$.

options.A: Emf is the terminal potential difference when no current is drawn; terminal potential difference is the potential difference when current is drawn. For a supplying cell, $V=\varepsilon-Ir$; $V=2.0-(0.5)(0.4)=1.8\,\text{V}$.
options.B: Emf is the terminal potential difference when current is drawn; $V=\varepsilon+Ir$; $V=2.2\,\text{V}$.
options.C: Emf and terminal potential difference are always identical; $V=\varepsilon=2.0\,\text{V}$.
